552	def _subtract_node(mem: dict, base: dict) -> dict:
553	    """Return the part of ``mem`` folded after ``base`` was taken."""
554	    kind = mem["kind"]
555	    if kind == "object":
556	        if _is_collapsed(mem):
557	            node = _collapsed_node("object")
558	            node["count"] = mem["count"] - base.get("count", 0)
559	            return node
560	        node = _new_node("object")
561	        node["count"] = mem["count"] - base.get("count", 0)
562	        base_fields = base.get("fields") or {}
563	        for name, entry in mem["fields"].items():
564	            base_entry = base_fields.get(name)
565	            if base_entry is None:
566	                node["fields"][name] = copy.deepcopy(entry)
567	            else:
568	                node["fields"][name] = _subtract_field(entry, base_entry)
569	        mem_overflow = mem.get("overflow")
570	        if mem_overflow is not None:
571	            base_overflow = base.get("overflow")
572	            if base_overflow is None:
573	                node["overflow"] = copy.deepcopy(mem_overflow)
574	            else:
575	                node["overflow"] = _subtract_field(mem_overflow, base_overflow)
576	        return node
577	    if kind == "array":
578	        node = _new_node("array")
579	        if mem.get("approximate"):
580	            node["approximate"] = True
581	        base_elements = base.get("elements") or {}
582	        for element_kind, child in mem["elements"].items():
583	            base_child = base_elements.get(element_kind)
584	            if base_child is None:
585	                node["elements"][element_kind] = copy.deepcopy(child)
586	            else:
587	                node["elements"][element_kind] = _subtract_node(child, base_child)
588	        return node
589	    return _new_node(kind)

592	def _subtract_field(mem: dict, base: dict) -> dict:
593	    entry = _new_field()
594	    entry["observed"] = mem["observed"] - base["observed"]
595	    if mem.get("approximate"):
596	        entry["approximate"] = True
597	    mem_names = mem.get("names")
598	    if mem_names is not None:
599	        # The delta cannot attribute provenance per name (only aggregate
600	        # counts are kept), so it carries every name its memory ever folded
601	        # in; the downstream merge is a union anyway, and over-inclusion
602	        # only ever widens validation for genuinely folded names.
603	        entry["names"] = sorted(mem_names)
604	    for kind, child in mem["types"].items():
605	        base_child = base["types"].get(kind)
606	        if base_child is None:
607	            entry["types"][kind] = copy.deepcopy(child)
608	        else:
609	            entry["types"][kind] = _subtract_node(child, base_child)
610	    return entry

613	def _join(path: str, name: str) -> str:
614	    # An identifier is joined with a dot; every other key is quoted in
615	    # brackets so a name containing a dot or a backslash can never be read
616	    # as a path separator: $["a.b"] is distinct from $.a.b.
617	    if name.isidentifier():
618	        return f"{path}.{name}"
619	    return f"{path}[{json.dumps(name)}]"

622	def _marker_path(path: str) -> str:
623	    """Render the overflow-marker location beneath an object node.
624	
625	    The marker can never be a real key (see ``OVERFLOW_MARKER``), so a bare
626	    ``.*`` segment cannot be produced by ``_join`` for any real field name;
627	    a field literally named "*" quotes as ``$["*"]`` and stays distinct.
628	    """
629	    return f"{path}.*"

632	def _check_object(node: dict, record: dict, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
633	    if _is_collapsed(node):
634	        # A depth-capped node tracked no fields, so nothing inside the
635	        # record's value can be checked; the approximation is marked in
636	        # the schema instead of guessed about here.
637	        return
638	    fields = node["fields"]
639	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
640	    overflow_names = None if overflow is None else overflow.get("names")
641	    for name in record:
642	        if name not in fields:
643	            if overflow is not None and (
644	                overflow_names is None or name in overflow_names
645	            ):
646	                # Only names that really folded into the overflow entry are
647	                # checked against its widened type set; ``names is None``
648	                # marks a legacy overflow entry with unknown provenance. A
649	                # name never seen before is still unexpected.
650	                _check_value(overflow["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)
651	            else:
652	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: unexpected field")
653	    for name, entry in fields.items():
654	        if name not in record:
655	            if not entry["optional"]:
656	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: missing required field")
657	            continue
658	        _check_value(entry["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)

661	def _check_value(types: dict, value: Any, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
662	    kind = _kind_of(value)
663	    node = types.get(kind)
664	    if node is None:
665	        expected = ", ".join(sorted(types))
666	        reports.append(f"{path}: type {kind} not in field types [{expected}]")
667	        return
668	    if kind == "object":
669	        _check_object(node, value, path, reports)
670	    elif kind == "array":
671	        for index, element in enumerate(value):
672	            _check_value(node["elements"], element, f"{path}[{index}]", reports)

675	# -- cross-revision compatibility -------------------------------------------
676	#
677	# Compatibility is read straight off the two committed schema trees, using
678	# exactly what ``check`` decides with: a record is accepted when every
679	# field it carries is a known (or genuinely overflow-folded) field whose
680	# value kind is in the entry's type set, every required field is present,
681	# and nested branches recurse. One symmetric walk therefore derives both
682	# directions at once: ``backward`` asks whether the new tree accepts every
683	# record the old tree accepts, ``forward`` the reverse.
684	#
685	# Each branch returns a ``(backward, forward)`` verdict pair. A branch
686	# either tree can only describe approximately - an overflow entry that may
687	# route the field, an entry flagged approximate, or a depth-capped subtree
688	# - is unknown in both directions and lists its source, in the same paths
689	# ``stats`` uses for approximated statistics (``$.*`` for an overflow
690	# entry, the subtree's own path for a collapsed node). The one exception
691	# is comparing a revision with itself: that revision is known to accept its
692	# own records, so ``Lens.compat`` answers compatible in both directions
693	# with no reasons after the revision has been read and validated.
694	
695	_COMPATIBLE = "compatible"
696	_BREAKING = "breaking"
697	_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
698	
699	# Witness recipe step tags (see ``_CompatDiffer``): an object field
700	# descent, one array-element nesting, a forced-kind leaf, and an omission
701	# of the innermost field.
702	_FIELD = "f"
703	_ARRAY = "a"
704	_KIND = "k"
705	_MISSING = "m"
706	
707	
708	def _combine_pair(pair: tuple[str, str], other: tuple[str, str]) -> tuple[str, str]:
709	    return (_worst(pair[0], other[0]), _worst(pair[1], other[1]))
710	
711	
712	def _worst(left: str, right: str) -> str:
713	    """Aggregate branch verdicts for one direction.
714	
715	    A branch that demonstrably rejects a legal record settles the
716	    direction as breaking even when another branch is unknowable; without
717	    one of those an unknown branch degrades it to unknown.
718	    """
719	    if left == _BREAKING or right == _BREAKING:
720	        return _BREAKING
721	    if left == _UNKNOWN or right == _UNKNOWN:
722	        return _UNKNOWN
723	    return _COMPATIBLE

726	def _overflow_live(entry: dict) -> bool:
727	    """Whether an overflow entry can route a field name during check.
728	
729	    An entry with known but empty provenance routes nothing; an explicit
730	    ``names: None`` (a pre-tracking overflow entry) routes any name.
731	    """
732	    names = entry.get("names", [])
733	    return names is None or bool(names)
734	
735	
736	def _overflow_routes(entry: dict | None, name: str) -> bool:
737	    if entry is None or not _overflow_live(entry):
738	        return False
739	    names = entry.get("names")
740	    return names is None or name in names

743	class _CompatDiffer:
744	    """Symmetric diff of two validated snapshots, aligned with ``check``."""
745	
746	    def __init__(self) -> None:
747	        self.changes: list[dict] = []
748	        self.reasons: set[str] = set()
749	        # One deterministic witness recipe per breaking pair position. Each
750	        # recipe is a tuple of tagged steps from the root object to that
751	        # position, so a record can be built straight from a schema tree
752	        # without matching change strings, re-deriving the alignment, or
753	        # risking a collision between a real field name and a step token:
754	        # ``("f", name)`` descends through an object field, ``("a",)``
755	        # through one array element nesting, and the terminal step is
756	        # either ``("k", kind)`` (force a value of that kind) or
757	        # ``("m",)`` (omit the innermost field).
758	        self.recipes: list[tuple[str, tuple]] = []
759	        self._steps: list[tuple] = []
760	
761	    @contextlib.contextmanager
762	    def _step(self, step: tuple) -> Iterator[None]:
763	        self._steps.append(step)
764	        try:
765	            yield
766	        finally:
767	            self._steps.pop()
768	
769	    def witness(self, direction: str, terminal: tuple) -> None:
770	        """Record a witness recipe for one breaking pair position.
771	
772	        ``direction`` names the accepting (record) side for the breaking
773	        direction being witnessed (``"old"`` for a backward-breaking
774	        position, ``"new"`` for a forward-breaking one); ``terminal`` is
775	        the recipe's terminal step. Every call site is a non-collapsed
776	        exact branch the accepting side demonstrably accepts.
777	        """
778	        self.recipes.append((direction, tuple(self._steps) + (terminal,)))
779	
780	    def diff(self, old_root: dict, new_root: dict) -> dict:
781	        backward, forward = self.compare_object(old_root, new_root, "$")
782	        self.changes.sort(key=lambda change: (change["path"], change["change"]))
783	        return {
784	            "backward": backward,
785	            "forward": forward,
786	            "changes": self.changes,
787	            "unknown_reasons": sorted(self.reasons),
788	        }
789	
790	    def change(self, path: str, category: str, breaking: bool) -> None:
791	        self.changes.append(
792	            {"path": path, "change": category, "breaking": breaking}
793	        )
794	
795	    def compare_object(self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
796	        if _is_collapsed(old) or _is_collapsed(new):
797	            # A depth-capped object lets anything nested through check, so
798	            # neither direction can be settled field by field.
799	            self.reasons.add(path)
800	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
801	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
802	        old_fields = old["fields"]
803	        new_fields = new["fields"]
804	        old_overflow = old.get("overflow")
805	        new_overflow = new.get("overflow")
806	        for name in sorted(set(old_fields) | set(new_fields)):
807	            field_path = _join(path, name)
808	            old_entry = old_fields.get(name)
809	            new_entry = new_fields.get(name)
810	            if old_entry is not None and new_entry is not None:
811	                with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
812	                    pair = self.compare_entry(old_entry, new_entry, field_path)
813	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, pair)
814	            elif old_entry is not None:
815	                # The field disappears from the new exact fields. New check
816	                # only accepts it when the name really folded into the new
817	                # overflow entry, whose merged type set is approximate.
818	                if _overflow_routes(new_overflow, name):
819	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
820	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
821	                else:
822	                    # New check rejects records carrying it; old records
823	                    # omitting it additionally fail an old required field
824	                    # under the forward direction.
825	                    self.change(field_path, "field_removed", True)
826	                    with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
827	                        # A legal new record omits it; the old
828	                        # required-field check reports it missing. That
829	                        # witness needs no value kind.
830	                        if not old_entry["optional"]:
831	                            self.witness("new", (_MISSING,))
832	                        kind = self._witness_present_kind(old_entry)
833	                        if kind is not None:
834	                            # A legal old record carries the field; new
835	                            # check reports it as unexpected.
836	                            self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
837	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
838	                        verdict,
839	                        (_BREAKING,
840	                         _BREAKING if not old_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE),
841	                    )
842	            else:
843	                # The field appears only among the new exact fields. Old
844	                # check accepts it only through its own overflow entry.
845	                if _overflow_routes(old_overflow, name):
846	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
847	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
848	                else:
849	                    # Backward: an old record omits it, so a new required
850	                    # field rejects that record while a new optional one
851	                    # lets it through. Forward: old check calls any record
852	                    # carrying it unexpected.
853	                    self.change(
854	                        field_path, "field_added", not new_entry["optional"]
855	                    )
856	                    with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
857	                        # A legal old record omits it; the new
858	                        # required-field check reports it missing.
859	                        if not new_entry["optional"]:
860	                            self.witness("old", (_MISSING,))
861	                        kind = self._witness_present_kind(new_entry)
862	                        if kind is not None:
863	                            # A legal new record carries the field; old
864	                            # check reports it as unexpected.
865	                            self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
866	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
867	                        verdict,
868	                        (_BREAKING if not new_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE,
869	                         _BREAKING),
870	                    )
871	        # A live overflow entry on either side folds names whose accepted
872	        # branches cannot be attributed exactly; every branch it governs is
873	        # unknown both ways. The marker can never be a real field name.
874	        for entry in (old_overflow, new_overflow):
875	            if entry is not None and _overflow_live(entry):
876	                self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
877	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
878	        return verdict

880	    @staticmethod
881	    def _witness_present_kind(entry: dict) -> str | None:
882	        """Deterministic kind a legal record uses for this exact entry.
883	
884	        Exact field entries compared here are never approximate, and a
885	        validated entry has observed at least one record, so its type set
886	        is non-empty. The fixed kind order (null, boolean, number, string,
887	        array, object) makes the choice independent of dict iteration
888	        order; scalars are preferred and an array precedes an object.
889	        """
890	        for kind in _KINDS:
891	            if kind in entry["types"]:
892	                return kind
893	        return None

895	    def compare_entry(
896	        self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str
897	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
898	        if old.get("approximate") or new.get("approximate"):
899	            # An entry flagged approximate absorbed overflow statistics in
900	            # an exact field position; its accepted value set cannot be
901	            # attributed precisely, so no change beneath it is asserted.
902	            self.reasons.add(path)
903	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
904	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
905	        if old["optional"] != new["optional"]:
906	            if old["optional"]:
907	                # Optional becomes required: old records may omit it. The
908	                # field name is the current innermost step; the missing
909	                # witness omits exactly that field.
910	                self.change(path, "optional_to_required", True)
911	                self.witness("old", (_MISSING,))
912	                verdict = (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE)
913	            else:
914	                # Required becomes optional: new records may omit it.
915	                self.change(path, "required_to_optional", False)
916	                self.witness("new", (_MISSING,))
917	                verdict = (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING)
918	        verdict = _combine_pair(
919	            verdict, self.compare_types(old["types"], new["types"], path, "type")
920	        )
921	        return verdict
922	
923	    def compare_types(
924	        self, old_types: dict, new_types: dict, path: str, prefix: str
925	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
926	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
927	        for kind in _KINDS:
928	            if kind not in old_types and kind not in new_types:
929	                continue
930	            old_node = old_types.get(kind)
931	            new_node = new_types.get(kind)
932	            if old_node is not None and new_node is not None:
933	                verdict = _combine_pair(
934	                    verdict, self.compare_kind(old_node, new_node, path)
935	                )
936	            elif old_node is not None:
937	                # Records of this kind are legal on the old side but the
938	                # new type set no longer contains it (narrowing). A record
939	                # forcing exactly this kind is the backward witness.
940	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_removed", True)
941	                self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
942	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE))
943	            else:
944	                # The new side widened with this kind; old check rejects
945	                # new records that take it (forward breaking), while old
946	                # records still pass the new, wider check.
947	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_added", False)
948	                self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
949	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING))
950	        return verdict
951	
952	    def compare_kind(
953	        self, old_node: dict, new_node: dict, path: str
954	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
955	        kind = old_node["kind"]
956	        if kind in ("null", "boolean", "number", "string"):
957	            return _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
958	        if kind == "object":
959	            return self.compare_object(old_node, new_node, path)
960	        return self.compare_arrays(old_node, new_node, path)

962	    def compare_arrays(
963	        self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str
964	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
965	        """Compare array element branches under one schema-level path.
966	
967	        check walks every element against the single merged element type
968	        set (a schema has no concrete indices), and it enforces that set
969	        even for a depth-capped array - only a collapsed *child* hides
970	        structure. So scalar element kinds gate exactly (rendered as
971	        ``path[]``) and collapsed element objects taint beneath them;
972	        element objects then join fields normally (``path[].name``). The
973	        matching array-level step marks the one nesting level check
974	        descends through per element.
975	        """
976	        element_path = f"{path}[]"
977	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
978	        for kind in _KINDS:
979	            if kind not in old["elements"] and kind not in new["elements"]:
980	                continue
981	            old_child = old["elements"].get(kind)
982	            new_child = new["elements"].get(kind)
983	            if old_child is not None and new_child is not None:
984	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
985	                    pair = self.compare_kind(old_child, new_child, element_path)
986	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, pair)
987	            elif old_child is not None:
988	                self.change(element_path, f"element_type_{kind}_removed", True)
989	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
990	                    self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
991	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE))
992	            else:
993	                self.change(element_path, f"element_type_{kind}_added", False)
994	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
995	                    self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
996	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING))
997	        return verdict

1007	# -- breaking-change witnesses ----------------------------------------------
1008	#
1009	# A witness for a breaking direction is one JSON object that the accepting
1010	# revision's ``check`` accepts (an empty report list) and the rejecting
1011	# revision's ``check`` rejects (the full, non-empty report list). The
1012	# differ records one recipe per breaking pair position while it walks; a
1013	# recipe is a tuple of tagged steps from the root object, and the builder
1014	# below turns each into a concrete, deterministic record straight off the
1015	# accepting revision's tree - it never parses change strings and never
1016	# invents fields, kinds or values the accepting schema has not observed.
1017	# Required sibling fields are filled along the way so the record is legal

1121	        node = types["object"]

1195	# -- field migration preview -------------------------------------------------
1196	#
1197	# A migration rule is a small JSON object describing one field-level edit:
1198	# ``{"op": "rename", "path": [...], "to": name}`` moves a field's value to
1199	# a new sibling name, ``{"op": "drop", "path": [...]}`` removes a field,
1200	# and ``{"op": "default", "path": [...], "value": ...}`` fills a field that
1201	# is genuinely missing (a present ``null`` is a value and is kept). The
1202	# path is a non-empty array whose string segments are literal field names
1203	# (a name containing a dot names one field, never a descent) and whose
1204	# ``null`` segments select every element of the array at that position;
1205	# the last segment is always a string naming the field the op edits.
1206	# Rules apply in order, each to the result of the previous one. A parent
1207	# that is simply missing skips the rule for that branch - parents are
1208	# never created - while a string segment meeting a non-object or a null
1209	# segment meeting a non-array is a structural ``ValueError``, as is a
1210	# rename whose target field already exists.
1211	
1212	_MIGRATION_OPS = ("rename", "drop", "default")
1213

1215	def _require_json_value(value: Any, what: str) -> None:
1216	    """Reject anything JSON cannot represent, recursing into containers."""
1217	    if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, bool, int)):
1218	        return
1219	    if isinstance(value, float):
1220	        if math.isfinite(value):
1221	            return
1222	    elif isinstance(value, list):
1223	        for item in value:
1224	            _require_json_value(item, what)
1225	        return
1226	    elif isinstance(value, dict):
1227	        for key, item in value.items():
1228	            if not isinstance(key, str):
1229	                break
1230	            _require_json_value(item, what)
1231	        else:
1232	            return
1233	    raise ValueError(f"{what} must be a JSON value")

1236	def _parse_migration_rules(rules: Any, *, label: str = "migration rule") -> list[dict]:
1237	    """Validate the rule list structurally before anything is applied.
1238	
1239	    Every rule must be a JSON object carrying exactly the keys its op
1240	    needs - ``op`` and ``path`` for all three, ``to`` for rename,
1241	    ``value`` for default - with a non-empty path of string/null segments
1242	    ending in a string, a string rename target distinct from the source
1243	    field name, and a JSON default value. Anything else is a
1244	    ``ValueError`` raised before any revision is read or any rule runs.
1245	    ``label`` names the group in error messages so forward and rollback
1246	    rules are distinguishable in a roundtrip preview.
1247	    """
1248	    if not isinstance(rules, list):
1249	        raise ValueError(f"{label}s must be a JSON array")
1250	    for index, rule in enumerate(rules):
1251	        if not isinstance(rule, dict):
1252	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index} must be a JSON object")
1253	        op = rule.get("op")
1254	        if op not in _MIGRATION_OPS:
1255	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index}: unknown op {op!r}")
1256	        path = rule.get("path")
1257	        if (
1258	            not isinstance(path, list)
1259	            or not path
1260	            or any(
1261	                segment is not None and not isinstance(segment, str)
1262	                for segment in path
1263	            )
1264	            or not isinstance(path[-1], str)
1265	        ):
1266	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index}: invalid path")
1267	        expected = {"op", "path"}
1268	        if op == "rename":
1269	            expected.add("to")
1270	        elif op == "default":
1271	            expected.add("value")
1272	        if set(rule) != expected:
1273	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index}: invalid keys for {op}")
1274	        if op == "rename":
1275	            if not isinstance(rule["to"], str):
1276	                raise ValueError(
1277	                    f"{label} {index}: rename target must be a string"
1278	                )
1279	            if rule["to"] == path[-1]:
1280	                raise ValueError(
1281	                    f"{label} {index}: rename target equals the "
1282	                    "source field"
1283	                )
1284	        elif op == "default":
1285	            _require_json_value(rule["value"], f"{label} {index} value")

1289	def _migration_containers(record: dict, path: list) -> list:
1290	    """The containers the path's final segment applies to.
1291	
1292	    Navigates every segment but the last: a string segment descends into
1293	    the named field of an object (a missing field drops that branch
1294	    silently - parents are never created), a null segment spreads over
1295	    every element of an array (an empty array simply selects nothing).
1296	    A string segment meeting a non-object or a null segment meeting a
1297	    non-array is a structural ``ValueError``.
1298	    """
1299	    containers = [record]
1300	    for segment in path[:-1]:
1301	        following = []
1302	        for container in containers:
1303	            if segment is None:
1304	                if not isinstance(container, list):
1305	                    raise ValueError("null path segment requires an array")
1306	                following.extend(container)
1307	            else:
1308	                if not isinstance(container, dict):
1309	                    raise ValueError("string path segment requires an object")
1310	                if segment in container:
1311	                    following.append(container[segment])
1312	        if not following:
1313	            return []
1314	        containers = following
1315	    return containers

1318	def _apply_migration_rule(record: dict, rule: dict) -> None:
1319	    """Apply one already-validated rule to the working record in place."""

1323	        if not isinstance(container, dict):
1324	            raise ValueError("string path segment requires an object")
1325	        if op == "rename":
1326	            if last not in container:

1332	            # new name and the same input always yields the same order.
1333	            renamed = [
1334	                (to if key == last else key, value)
1335	                for key, value in container.items()
1336	            ]
1337	            container.clear()

1347	# -- rollback rehearsal ------------------------------------------------------
1348	#
1349	# After the forward migration preview succeeds, the rollback rules run on
1350	# the migrated record and the recovered object is checked against the old
1351	# revision and then compared structurally with the original record. The
1352	# comparison ignores object key order and compares objects key by key;
1353	# arrays of the same length compare element by element. A missing key
1354	# records that field's path; a type mismatch, an unequal array length or
1355	# unequal scalars record only the current position and never expand it.
1356	# Missing is distinct from null and booleans are distinct from numbers,
1357	# while ints and floats compare by numeric value. Paths reuse the check
1358	# field/array notation (``_join``) and are reported de-duplicated in
1359	# string order.

1363	    """The comparison kind, splitting booleans off from numbers."""
1364	    if value is None:
1365	        return "null"
1366	    if isinstance(value, bool):
1367	        return "boolean"
1368	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
1369	        return "number"
1370	    if isinstance(value, str):
1371	        return "string"
1372	    if isinstance(value, list):
1373	        return "array"
1374	    return "object"

1379	    if isinstance(left, bool) or isinstance(right, bool):
1380	        return left is right
1381	    return left == right

1384	def _structural_differences(original: Any, recovered: Any, path: str) -> list[str]:
1385	    """Every path at which two JSON values differ, check path notation."""
1386	    left_kind = _json_kind(original)
1387	    right_kind = _json_kind(recovered)
1388	    if left_kind != right_kind:
1389	        # A type difference (missing vs null, boolean vs number included)
1390	        # is terminal at the current position.
1391	        return [path]
1392	    if left_kind == "object":
1393	        differences: list[str] = []
1394	        for name in sorted(set(original) | set(recovered)):
1395	            field_path = _join(path, name)
1396	            if name not in original or name not in recovered:
1397	                # A key one side lacks names exactly that field path.
1398	                differences.append(field_path)
1399	            else:
1400	                differences.extend(
1401	                    _structural_differences(
1402	                        original[name], recovered[name], field_path
1403	                    )
1404	                )
1405	        return differences
1406	    if left_kind == "array":
1407	        if len(original) != len(recovered):
1408	            return [path]
1409	        differences = []
1410	        for index, (left_element, right_element) in enumerate(
1411	            zip(original, recovered)
1412	        ):
1413	            differences.extend(
1414	                _structural_differences(
1415	                    left_element, right_element, f"{path}[{index}]"
1416	                )
1417	            )
1418	        return differences
1419	    if _scalars_equal(original, recovered):
1420	        return []
1421	    return [path]

1558	    """Write text atomically: a crash leaves only the old or new file."""
1559	    tmp = file_path.with_name(file_path.name + ".tmp")
1560	    fd = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o644)
1561	    try:
1562	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
1563	            handle.write(text)
1564	            handle.flush()
1565	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
1566	        os.replace(tmp, file_path)
1567	    except BaseException:
1568	        try:
1569	            os.unlink(tmp)
1570	        except OSError:
1571	            pass
